strategy.title: No executable plan: the trucking PM workbook has no evidenced price
strategy.why: The only opening's price fact ($1,200) describes HVAC contractors paying for a per-technician field-service software seat per year, not regional trucking fleet managers buying a preventive-maintenance scheduling workbook. A price from another population and another product is not evidence of what this buyer pays, so the offer, the deal count needed for $5,000 and the economics are all unestablished.

alternatives.title: Sell the workbook at the card's $1,200 (5 deals) to fleet managers by email
alternatives.why: Rejected: the $1,200 figure is an HVAC software-seat price, a mismatched population and product; counting on it would be an assumption, not evidence.

steps.label: Establish what regional trucking fleet managers actually pay for a preventive-maintenance scheduling workbook/template (published prices with source and date)
Quote the workbook at a stated price to fleet managers via published business email and record paid pre-orders at that price

quantities.name: price
quantities.needs: A published price paid by regional trucking fleets for a PM scheduling workbook, or paid pre-orders at a quoted price

sources.claim: Software Advice analyzed data from HVAC contractors: field-service management software for HVAC businesses costs $1,200 a year per technician seat.
sources.population: HVAC contractors buying field-service software seats

sources.claim: 600 regional trucking fleets hold state motor-carrier permits; each schedules preventive maintenance monthly.

noPlan.decisiveGap: OFFER_AND_PRICE: no evidenced price that regional trucking fleet managers pay for a preventive-maintenance scheduling workbook; the card's $1,200 is an HVAC field-service software seat price (different buyers, different product), so neither the deal count for $5,000 nor the economics can be established.
noPlan.resolution: Research published prices for trucking PM scheduling workbooks/templates paid by fleet managers (source + date), or quote a price to fleet managers via their published business emails and record paid pre-orders at that price; re-plan once a matching price is recorded on the card.
